notes: Provenance policy for honoring accepted OSC 52 clipboard writes. A write reaches the system clipboard only when an unconsumed trusted user gesture no older than max_gesture_age_ms exists at the moment the write is delivered, and delivering the write consumes that gesture. Terminal output can never create, extend, or stand in for a gesture, and never refreshes the gesture deadline. Steps replay in order: 'gesture' records a trusted one-shot user gesture, 'revoke' withdraws any standing grant, 'terminal-output' is arbitrary non-gesture terminal activity, 'advance-within-gesture-age' advances the clock by less than max_gesture_age_ms, 'advance-past-gesture-age' advances the clock beyond max_gesture_age_ms, and 'osc52-write' is one policy-accepted OSC 52 write. expected_writes gives the allow/deny decision for each osc52-write step in order. known_gaps lists consumers whose current implementation is known to diverge; those consumers must fail the contract expectation until the gap is fixed and the entry removed.

known_gaps.ghosthub-terminal: Workers initialize the presentation clipboard gate enabled before any gesture, so a write delivered in the initial generation is honored.
The presentation clipboard gate is an enabled window, not a one-shot grant; every write inside the window is honored.
Workers initialize the presentation clipboard gate enabled before any gesture, so terminal output followed by a write in the initial generation is honored.
The presentation clipboard gate has no clock; a grant never expires until the gate is advanced.
The presentation clipboard gate has no clock; terminal output cannot refresh a deadline that does not exist, but the unexpired window still honors the write.
